Container handles

Source: R/container.R
containers.Rd

A document's data lives in containers. doc_text(), doc_map(), doc_list(), doc_movable_list(), doc_counter(), and doc_tree() return a handle to the root container with the given name, creating it on first use. Handles to nested containers come from map_set_container(), list_insert_container(), map_get(), and list_get().

A handle is a loro_text, loro_map, loro_list, loro_movable_list, loro_counter, or loro_tree object. Like a loro_doc, it has reference semantics: editing through a handle changes the document it belongs to.

  • container_value() returns the contents of a container: a string for text, a number for a counter, and a list for a map or list. A tree is a list of its root nodes, each a list with id, parent (NA at the top level), a 1-based index, a fractional_index (Loro's internal sort key), meta, and children (a list of nodes of the same form). Nested containers are expanded to their contents by default; with deep = FALSE they appear as container id strings.

  • container_is_deleted() reports whether the container has been removed from its document, for example because its key was overwritten or its parent deleted. A handle to a deleted container can still be read, but editing through it is an error.

  • container_id() returns the container's unique id as a string.

Handles also answer to the base functions that fit them: length() for text, maps, and lists, names(), $, and [[ for maps, [[ for lists, as.character() for text, and as.list() for maps and lists.

A document can be passed wherever a text, map, list, counter, or tree handle is expected. It stands for its root container of that type under the default name, so text_insert(doc, 1, "Hello") is text_insert(doc_text(doc), 1, "Hello") and map_set(doc, a = 1) is map_set(doc_map(doc), a = 1). This is convenient for a document that holds one container of a kind; use handles for named or nested containers and for movable lists.

Root container names are shared across types within a document's value, so use distinct names for different root containers: if two root containers of different types have the same name, each keeps its own contents but doc_value() shows only one of them.

Asking for a root container creates it. Once doc_map(doc, "notes") has been called, doc_value() includes an empty notes entry, on this replica and on any that later import from it, even if nothing is ever stored there. Two replicas with the same edits can therefore differ in which empty root containers their values list.

Usage

doc_text(doc, name = "text")

doc_map(doc, name = "map")

doc_list(doc, name = "list")

doc_movable_list(doc, name = "list")

doc_counter(doc, name = "counter")

doc_tree(doc, name = "tree")

container_value(x, deep = TRUE)

container_is_deleted(x)

container_id(x)

Arguments

doc

A loro_doc.

name

Name of the root container.

x

A container handle.

deep

Whether to expand nested containers.

Value

doc_text(), doc_map(), doc_list(), doc_movable_list(), doc_counter(), and doc_tree() return container handles; container_value() returns a string, number, or list; container_id() returns a string; and container_is_deleted() returns a logical.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()

text = doc_text(doc, "body")
text_insert(text, 1, "Hello")

meta = doc_map(doc, "meta")
map_set(meta, title = "Greeting")

container_value(meta)
#> $title
#> [1] "Greeting"
#> 
container_id(text)
#> [1] "cid:root-body:Text"
doc_value(doc)
#> $body
#> [1] "Hello"
#> 
#> $meta
#> $meta$title
#> [1] "Greeting"
#> 
#>
